newsitem.title: USA: Borders says Q1 improves on sales, margins.
newsitem.headline: Borders says Q1 improves on sales, margins.

text.p: Borders Group Inc said an improvement in first quarter earnings was due to strong sales at both Borders and Waldenbooks, as well as favorable gross margin and expense controls, offset in part by strategic spending on new growth initiatives.

"The positive sales results allowed us to accelerate strategic spending on growth initiatives during the first quarter, and we look forward to delivering a strong return on that investment in the future," said chairman and chief executive Robert Di Romualdo.
The company reported net income of $0.4 million or $0.00 per share as compared with a loss of $3.4 million or $0.04 per share for the first quarter of fiscal 1996.

Borders reported a 30.7 percent increase in sales for the Borders superstores to $266.3 million versus $203.8 million for the year-ago period and a 1.4 percent decline in Waldenbooks sales to $197.3 million versus $200.2 million during the first quarter of 1996. The company said the sales decline at Waldenbooks reflects a comparable store sales increase of 1.1 percent, offset by a decrease in the number of stores from the prior year.

Borders attributed its increase in gross margin to continued improvements in distribution and inventory shrinkage results, improved merchandise mix management and a decline in occupancy expense as a percentage of sales due to both the continued maturation of the Borders stores and the continued shift in sales base from mall stores to superstores.
In line with this shift the company closed more than 30 Walden Mall Book Stores during the quarter and opened six Borders Superstores. It opened one Walden Mall Store.
Consolidated sales for the quarter were $463.6 million, a 14.8 percent increase over the prior year's $404.0 million.
Consolidated gross margin grew from 23.1 percent of sales for the first quarter of fiscal 1996 to 24.3 percent for the first quarter of fiscal 1997.
